All four A frames come from the same build and HUD and show the same city: shophouse rows, slab apartment blocks, rain trees, yellow-box junctions and a hazy skyline. Their warm low-sun lighting and building silhouettes are good, so the art direction is promising. What sinks them is a set of problems that repeat and can be fixed. (1) The asphalt material is the most repeated tell: a static white salt-and-pepper speckle with blotchy shadows fills the lower half of every frame. (2) The cars look unfinished: the paint is matte or faceted with no crisp reflections, and tail lights and headlights blow out into large bloom blobs. (3) The driving frames do not show speed: at 70–83 km/h there is no road motion blur or streaking. (4) There is little life: junctions are nearly empty, with one or two cars and few pedestrians. (5) There are low-poly planters, flat untextured ground lots and a placeholder grey-grid minimap. The B frames are older, softer, heavily graded marketing-style captures, yet they still win on hero-car materials, clean road surfaces, density and deliberate composition. Only pair 2's dusk neon shot genuinely wowed. The suggested fix order is: road material and anti-aliasing, then car paint and lamp bloom, then speed blur, then traffic and pedestrian density. Note that three of the four B images carry a visible game-logo watermark, so this comparison was not fully blind. The verdicts rest on the visible quality differences listed per pair.
